# P13 extension: local slope adaptation across course presentations

This development experiment uses the previously evaluated OULAD 2014J presentation. Treat each course module as a simulated horizontal client. Fit on eligible registrations from 2013B, 2013J and 2014B after excluding every 2014J learner. Score eligible 2014J registrations in modules with training records. Define registration and withdrawal eligibility as in the day-60 audit. The four available activity measures are clicks, active days, resources, and recency. Map each nonnegative count to log1p(count)/4 without exchanging moments, and append an intercept. Predict the released final Withdrawn status.

Use a zero-initialized logistic model, 40 synchronous rounds, full client participation, five full-batch local gradient steps per round, step size 0.25. FedAvg weights clients by registrations. FedProx adds a squared proximal penalty with coefficient 0.1 around the broadcast model. Compare centralized full-batch gradient descent, independent local fits, and a pooled depth-4 GPU CatBoost. The candidate takes one local penalized Newton step from the final FedAvg parameters using only training rows. Fix ridge at 0.02 on slopes and 0.005 on intercept. Compare with intercept-only adjustment and a weak-ridge (1e-5) local Newton step with the same data. All local post-training adaptations use the same uploaded model sequence and one final broadcast. Count 40 upload vectors and 41 download vectors per client, including final distribution. Treat these as payload equivalents in a simulation. Each client refreshes once at evaluation time with its own previously fitted update. No later-term outcomes enter these fits.

Predefine the exploratory advancement threshold as +.02 absolute module-macro ROC AUC against every comparator, the primary practical margin used in P13. Report individual module losses/AUCs and macro and pooled scores. The current cohort has already been used for other analyses. Scientific confirmation would require a fresh cohort, nearest published personalized FL methods, time-window boosting and a temporal neural comparator. No differential privacy, deployment or real cross-institution federation is tested.
